section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section reviews existing literature on the relationship between sexual orientation and body image in women, highlighting inconsistencies in prior research comparing lesbian and heterosexual women. The authors argue for the importance of including bisexual and queer-identified women in body image research and propose that body appreciation—a multidimensional measure of positive body appraisal—may better capture differences across sexual orientation groups than traditional body satisfaction measures. The section concludes by presenting two hypotheses to be tested in the current study regarding body appreciation differences by sexual orientation while controlling for demographic and physical characteristics.
